description: Checks smoke fails in owners-shared mode; labels-off it fails none.

categories.reason: A server in owner mode refuses CONFIG SET aof-use-rdb-preamble no, because the base of its append-only file is always a snapshot (see The append-only file in docs/persistence.md). So smoke's check that switches the preamble off differs, the check of CONFIG GET and SET of every parameter differs in that one parameter, and after the two rewrites the base of the log is still a base.rdb file where the reference has a base.aof. Every record of the log also starts with the scope of the change, here a LABEL AS head with the marking (the default login is an operator that names no owner, so no owner word follows), so the four checks that read the last lines of the log as plain commands find the head in front of each write: the transaction wrapped in one MULTI and EXEC, the single write that is not wrapped, the transactions that write nothing, and the transaction that selects another database inside MULTI.

categories.reason: MIGRATE answers ERR MIGRATE is off while a label scheme is configured; move keys with DUMP and RESTORE on a server in owner mode, because it would write at whatever login its cached connection to the target holds. The two scripted MIGRATE comparisons, from Eski into the reference and from Eski into a second Eski, run every case and differ in each one whose reply, dirty counters or later state the refused MIGRATE changes: the replies, the keys left on both sides, the cached connections and the read timeout case, which answers at once. The single MIGRATE checks against the second Eski and the closed port check differ for the same reason, and MONITOR, which shows only commands that arrive, does not show the refused MIGRATE commands of the redaction check.

categories.reason: RESTORE on a server in owner mode always checks its payload in depth, whatever sanitize-dump-payload says, because every writer may restore there. The dump cases that restore, with sanitize-dump-payload at no, a payload that only the deep check refuses, the 24-byte set y9, an intset whose members are out of order, and a set listpack with a repeated member, answer ERR Bad data format, so the state of y9 after them differs too, and so do the two corrupt payload cases that restore a set with repeated elements without sanitizing.

categories.reason: A login created without a clearance rule runs at the lowest label, and without an owner rule it acts as SHARED without the operator scope (see Logins in docs/owners.md). The gate keeps the default login, an operator without an owner rule, at the top label through the ACL scenarios, so the permissions scenario writes shared keys and publishes at the top label, which its new logins do not dominate. Their reads answer nil or empty, their key counts read 0 and their subscribers receive none of the published messages; the two protocols differ the same way.

categories.reason: ACL GETUSER adds the clearance, trust, token-keys and owners fields and the owner-shared and owner-operator flags, and ACL LIST carries the label and owner rules, so every ACL scenario that reads a login back differs from its first GETUSER on. categories.reason: Owner mode turns the label machinery on, so the server keeps the watched keys of a transaction that a write has marked until the watches are cleared, adds the keys of a WATCH sent after the mark and keeps queueing the commands of a marked transaction, so that the watch count, the transaction fields and the client memory of a connection do not depend on whether a watched key was written; the 7.4 server forgets the keys, ignores the WATCH and stops queueing. The introspection scenario writes keys its connections watch and then reads the watch, multi and multi-mem fields of CLIENT LIST and the watching_clients and total_watched_keys of INFO, which therefore differ after each such write.
